title: Try to Rule Fairly and You'll Be Overthrown
beats: Do you want to rule and fix your country?
Why do rulers act selfishly and stupidly? Are they dumb, or is it something else?
No man rules alone; power means getting others to act; defines keys to power
Dictatorship: maybe a dozen keys; displease them and you are replaced
All countries lie on a spectrum of few to many keys
Rule 1: get the keys. Rule 2: control the treasure
Benevolent spending on citizens is treasure a rival can promise to your keys
Keys face the same problem one level down; smart keys watch the balance
Self-sustaining core: court raises treasure to keep the court loyal
More keys means shorter reigns; Rule 3: minimize keys; why new dictators purge allies
Summarizes dictator success, turns to democracy
Democracy: no man rules alone again; power fractured
Voters as blocks; rewarded as groups; farm subsidies example
Rule 3 in democracy: non-voting blocks ignored, gerrymandering, voting rules
Big individual keys get loopholes and contracts, not gold
Contradictory-looking policy explained as balancing keys
Why not just bribe the army? Turn to taxes and revolts
Graph: tax rate vs number of keys; more democracy, lower taxes
Low-earners pull average down; dictators take wealth directly
Democracies are better not because rulers are better but because incentives align with productivity
Resource-rich dictatorships: gold or oil needs no citizens
Middling dictators: people storm the palace only when the army lets them
Why democracies resist coups: competing keys, destroyed productivity, coup cull gamble
More wealth from citizens, more spread power; democracies fall when poor or resource-found
Rules apply to CEOs, HOA chairs; war, aid, corruption later
Zeroth rule: without power you affect nothing; maybe you will be different

metrics.misconception: yes: rulers are stupid or evil (0:15, 12:10); people overthrow dictators (14:04)
metrics.examples: one running model applied to dictatorship, then democracy, then resource states, then CEOs/HOAs; grows from a dozen keys to millions of voters to all organizations
metrics.ending: Generalization to all power structures, zeroth rule, return to second-person aspiring ruler

principles.2: confirmed: only one invented term (keys to power, 1:04) carries the whole video
principles.3: confirmed: the three numbered rules are reapplied to each new regime 7:45, 8:03
principles.4: partly: voters-as-blocks (6:57) reduces democracy to the dictator model
principles.5: confirmed: viewer cast as aspiring ruler throughout 0:00, 6:11, 17:37
principles.6: partly: simplest regime (dictatorship, dozen keys) first, democracy second
principles.7: confirmed: same rules recur so viewer predicts democracy behavior before told 6:57-8:36
principles.8: partly: section breaks with music cues (0:31, 6:11, 10:29) act as pacing resets
principles.9: confirmed: rules repeated across dictatorship, democracy, resource states
principles.10: confirmed: dozen keys to millions of voters to all organizations
principles.11: confirmed: keys, then treasure, then minimize keys, then taxes builds on rule 2

new_moves.name: new:single-model-reapplied
new_moves.what: Introduce one compact model then rerun it on progressively different systems so each is a prediction test

new_moves.name: new:numbered-rule-with-zeroth
new_moves.what: End by adding a 'zeroth' rule that reframes the list as applying to the viewer

new_moves.name: new:valley-diagram
new_moves.what: Two stable extremes with an unstable middle as a memorable shape

new_moves.name: new:music-section-cues
new_moves.what: Distinct music marks each part as a chapter break

theory: One small model (keys, treasure, three rules) is introduced early and then replayed on dictatorship, democracy, resource states and corporations, so every new section is a prediction exercise rather than new material. The repeated surprise 'it is incentives, not character' resolves the opening paradox and is what makes the model stick.
velocity: Orchestrator: playbook 'model then replay': teach a 3-rule model once, then cycle domains asking the learner to predict
Learner model: track whether the learner can apply the model unprompted in a new domain as the mastery signal
Scene builder: persistent rule-list sidebar that highlights the rule in use per domain
Voice: chapter transitions with a distinct audio/visual cue on regime switches
Evals: flag claims supported only by assertion; Grey's single graph shows how sparse evidence can be
